page: Amazon Web Services r8a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 4.5 GHz with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8a.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance across CPU and memory subsystems. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the top 10% of benchmarked hardware. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with uncached read speeds reaching 423.16 GB/sec and write speeds at 211.24 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a Passmark database score in the top 10% and Redis SET operations achieving 193.5 million operations per second. The processor's instruction set includes AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration, which support high-throughput tasks like bzip3 decompression and static web serving.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r8a.16xlarge offers high resource density, combining a large DDR5 memory footprint with dedicated, high-frequency AMD EPYC cores. This makes it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads without sacrificing compute performance. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. The instance is configured for large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
